title: Which muscles, and when: space-by-time (sNM3F) muscle synergies from real forearm EMG

dataset.name: GRABMyo (Gesture Recognition and Biometrics ElectroMyogram)
dataset.record: session 1, participant 1, 16 forearm channels; 2 gestures x 7 trials; 20-450 Hz bandpass, rectified, 8 Hz envelope, per-muscle normalised, time-normalised to 60 points
dataset.citation: Pradhan A, He J, Jiang N. Multi-day dataset of forearm and wrist electromyogram for hand gesture recognition and biometrics. Sci Data 2022; PhysioNet doi:10.13026/rd4p-4w49.

proposition: Spatial NMF asks WHICH muscles group; space-by-time (sNM3F) also asks WHEN. On real forearm EMG the ecosystem factorises each trial's 16-muscle x 60-time envelope (960 values) into a few SHARED spatial modules and SHARED temporal modules plus a tiny per-trial activation matrix: a 2x2 model (4 shared modules) reconstructs the multi-trial EMG at VAF 0.958, and a 3x3 model at 0.968 -- so each trial is compressed to just a handful of activation coefficients over common modules, and those activations carry the gesture above chance (leave-one-out accuracy 0.64 vs 0.50).

claims.statement: reconstruction VAF of the 2 spatial x 2 temporal model
VAF of the single spatial x single temporal model
VAF of the 3 spatial x 3 temporal model
leave-one-out gesture accuracy from the activation coefficients

validation.reference: The sample-based non-negative matrix tri-factorisation (sNM3F; Delis et al. 2014) reconstructs a set of muscle x time EMG trials from a SMALL number of shared spatial modules (which muscles co-activate) and shared temporal modules (when), combined by a per-trial activation matrix -- achieving high variance-accounted-for with few modules, and with the activations carrying task identity. A correct implementation must (1) reach high VAF with a compact model, (2) increase VAF monotonically with module count, and (3) let the activations discriminate the task above chance.
validation.data: REAL -- GRABMyo (PhysioNet), 16 forearm EMG channels, 2 gestures x 7 trials
validation.note: The headline is COMPRESSION with interpretable structure: a 2x2 model -- two shared spatial modules (16x2) and two shared temporal modules (60x2) common to all 14 trials, plus a per-trial 2x2 activation -- reconstructs each trial's 960-value EMG at 0.958 VAF, so a new trial adds only four numbers. VAF rises monotonically (0.930 / 0.958 / 0.968 / 0.973 for 1..4 modules, vaf_curve.csv). Honest scope: the activation-based gesture discrimination is MODEST (leave-one-out 0.64 vs 0.50 chance) because only two similar gestures x seven trials from one participant are used -- it shows the activations carry task information, not a strong classifier; more gestures/participants would sharpen it. The spatial/temporal modules are shared by construction; the task-specificity lives in the activations, which is the sNM3F design.

open_questions.q: With more gestures and participants the activation coefficients should separate tasks much more sharply (a decoding case in its own right), and the shared spatial/temporal modules could be tested for cross-participant invariance. Documented, not escalated.
